title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.33687v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealing failures in both evidence reading and downstream question answering. translated_title: 先阅读后使用：改进视觉-语言模型中的视觉记忆利用
translated_abstract: 多模态记忆使长时程视觉-语言智能体能够保存并检索过去的经验。虽然先前的研究主要集中在记忆的构建与检索上，但如何有效地利用所提供的记忆，对视觉-语言模型（VLM）而言仍是一个挑战。我们发现，即使提供了充分的多模态证据，VLM也常常无法回答下游问题。为了探究VLM为何会陷入困境，我们将记忆图像替换为参考字幕，并观察到显著的性能提升，这表明模型在直接读取视觉证据方面存在困难。然而，模型生成的字幕可能遗漏关键信息，限制了该方法在实际中的应用。这些局限性促使我们更深入地审视记忆利用问题，揭示了在证据阅读和下游问题回答两个环节中均存在失败。基于这一区分，我们提出了MemRU，这是一个两阶段训练框架，通过……来改进证据阅读能力（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出MemRU两阶段训练框架，通过区分“证据阅读”与“问题回答”两个失败环节并强化模型读取视觉证据的能力，来改进视觉-语言模型对多模态记忆的有效利用。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes MemRU, a two-stage training framework that improves vision-language models' utilization of multimodal memory by distinguishing and addressing failures in both evidence reading and downstream question answering.
